Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — MediCorps is running a compliance carveout for our EU inference flows and we need to validate a few operational controls before we can sign the DPA addendum. High level asks: can you confirm (1) EU-only processing for inference (including any caches/KV), (2) backup lifecycle and whether copies ever transit outside the EU, (3) operator access model for on-call SREs / support (just-in-time, approvals, full session logging), and (4) what evidence Redwood can provide to prove deletion (active store + backups + snapshots + subprocessor flows)?

We also need a mapping of SCC clauses (Annex I/II/III where applicable) to the technical controls you actually operate. If you already have a short runbook or a one-page flow diagram showing in-region storage, replication, and deletion, that would be ideal.

Can we do a 30-min call next week? Privacy would like the artifacts before the call so they can prepare questions.

Thanks,
Elena

Hi Elena — good to meet you over email. Appreciate the clear ask. Quick answers and next steps:

- We support EU-only inference by routing inference requests to customer-dedicated clusters in EU regions and by default store model KV caches and temporary context in-region.
- Backups are written to EU-only object storage; there is no cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled by the customer.
- Operator access is JIT + RBAC with time-limited elevation and audited console/session recording.
- We can provide deletion attestations and a sample audit log showing deletion markers and retention lifecycle events.

Naomi will attach the runbook and an SCCs mapping spreadsheet. Can you confirm scope: are you validating inference-only (requests + context + logs) or also any training-stage artifacts / model uploads?

Propose a 30-min call on Tue 20 Jul 09:00 CET to walk through artifacts and any follow-ups from Privacy. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,

Subject: RE: Operational controls for EU-exclusive inference — SCCs & retention walkthrough

Hi Elena / Karthik,

Dropping in a bit more technical detail and attaching the items Karthik mentioned. Attachments (stubs): EU-processing-flow_v2.pdf, SCCs-AnnexA-mapping.xlsx, redline_SCCs_response.docx. Highlights below so Privacy can triage quickly: 

1) EU-only routing and storage
- Inference traffic is routed by region tag at the edge and bound to a dedicated EU cluster when the customer enables EU-only processing. KV caches and ephemeral session caches are kept on local NVMe attached to the EU hosts; no async replication to non-EU regions.

2) Backups and lifecycle
- Backups are stored in EU-only object buckets and encrypted with a customer-scoped KMS key. Default backup retention is 30 days; this is configurable down to 0 (no backups) or up to 365 days per contract.
- Cold vault export: we only export to cold archives outside the EU if explicitly enabled; for MediCorps we recommend keeping cold archives in-region.

3) Operator access and auditability
- Access model: RBAC + JIT ephemeral sessions via our access broker. Any elevated session requires approval from SRE lead and creates a session record, keystroke-level command logs where permitted, and a time-bounded token.
- Third-party subprocessors (managed storage, monitoring) are contractually restricted from accessing production data without a customer authorisation workflow.

4) Deletion proof and retention enforcement
- We can provide deletion attestations showing API delete calls, S3 delete markers, lifecycle transitions, and snapshots purge logs. For backups, we retain a deletion audit that shows backup manifest removal and KMS key rotation entries.
- Note: legal holds/forensic hold requests can extend retention temporarily; we will surface the exact operational steps in the runbook.

Open items we need from MediCorps:
- Confirm scope: inference runtime + logs only (no model training artifacts)
- Any minimum backup retention requirement >30 days
- Whether you require a signed attestation template or an annexed DPA clause.

I attached the SCC mapping and a short processing flow diagram. Happy to review live on the call.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Privacy Engineer — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

- Deletion evidence: can you provide an example log extract that shows (a) API delete call, (b) backup manifest deletion, and (c) KMS key rotation entry (redacted is fine)? Privacy wants to understand whether those three artefacts could be stitched together into a single attestation.

We can do Tue 20 Jul 09:00 CET for the call — please send an invite. We’ll aim to have Privacy and Legal on the line.

Best,
Elena
